findings.finding: INFO 207 says the laws and protections differ by loan purpose, and that the law provides the lowest level of protection to commercial loans, including loans to small businesses. Both sentences match the information sheet. The second sentence follows the ASIC attribution rather than sitting inside the 'explains that' clause.

business.gov.au says loans vary a lot in their costs and conditions, including loan term, interest rate, and set-up costs and ongoing fees, and that it is a good idea to compare loan products from multiple lenders before applying. The page omits 'a lot', writes 'setup', and expands It's to 'it is'. The official page title is Apply for a business loan; the anchor calls it a business loan preparation guide. The cited facts are on that page.

The answer-first definition is restated in the at-a-glance table and the first FAQ. The FAQ document list after 'Documentation requirements vary between loans.' is hedged industry practice ('commonly request'), not the business.gov.au paperwork list. 'Most lenders want to see that the borrower has real equity at risk' is unsourced general practice, not a statistic.
